title: The supplied strict reduction has a normalized universal counit
statement: Fix the finite-field datum, $\ell\ne p$, $E$ and finite-type $W$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $S$ be a supplied coefficient calculus with its coherence [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] and $O$ ordinary quotient-sequence adjoints [def-pur-sequence-adjoint-resolution-data]. There exists a counit $\epsilon:Q\mathcal R\to O^*Q$ making the supplied reduction $\mathcal R$ itself a universal left-derived functor of ordinary pullback. For every flat-term K-flat complex $P$, $\epsilon_P$ is the hom of an isomorphism whose actual finite and quotient-transition identifications satisfy CoefficientReductionPresentation [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. No resolution comparisons or derived shift comparisons are asserted.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] to the constant-system projection O.p. Its ordinary inverse image is B tensor_(cA) c(-). The fixed description [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site] restricts this sheaf tensor at each n to the ordinary tensor over A; [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and O.tensor identify it with Q tensor_A B_n. O.tensor_transition identifies its actual horizontal maps with the quotient transitions. The universal counit is invertible on flat-term K-flat representatives.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] every input has a flat-term K-flat resolution. Apply [lem-sp-strict-coefficient-tensor-descent] to the coefficient quotients and their transition maps. The normalization in the supplied coherent calculus [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] identifies its reduction with this unique resolving descent, including finite evaluations and horizontal transitions. Transfer the universal counit from step 1 across this normalized comparison to S.reduction. Universality is invariant under that isomorphism. On each flat-term K-flat representative the counit is an isomorphism, and the normalized finite and transition identifications are precisely CoefficientReductionPresentation with O.tensor. This gives the counit and all assertions, without claiming resolution-comparison or shift data.
